title: Mango Mousse
subtitle: Tropical mango purée folded through whipped cream and set lightly
excerpt: Fresh mango puréed and folded through whipped cream with a little gelatine to hold its shape. The colour is vivid yellow-orange and the flavour is full and tropical. Chill for at least 2 hours.
sourceNotes: Mango mousse is widely made across South Asian and Southeast Asian home cooking, often with condensed milk or cream. The British version, a French-style cream mousse with mango purée, became popular in the UK from the 1990s as fresh mangoes became more widely available in supermarkets.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to a day ahead and keep covered in the fridge.

content.text: Mango mousse is puréed fresh mango folded through softly whipped cream, set with a little gelatine so it holds its shape overnight. The colour when made with ripe Alphonso or Ataulfo mangoes is a vivid deep orange; the texture is light and airy but with a full, almost jammy mango flavour throughout. Choose the ripest mangoes you can find, the flavour of the mousse depends entirely on the fruit quality.

items.prepNote: peeled and diced, about 400g prepared flesh

content.text: Blend the diced mango with the caster sugar and lemon juice until completely smooth. Pass through a sieve if you want a very fine texture, or leave as-is for a slightly more textured result. You should have around 350ml of purée.

Soak the gelatine leaves in cold water for 5 minutes until soft. Warm 3 tablespoons of the mango purée in a small saucepan over a low heat until just steaming, do not boil. Squeeze the excess water from the gelatine leaves and stir them into the warm purée until fully dissolved. Pour the dissolved gelatine mixture back into the remaining mango purée and stir to combine. Leave to cool for 10 minutes.

Whip the double cream in a large bowl to soft peaks. Fold the mango purée into the whipped cream in three additions, using a large metal spoon and folding gently until just combined and uniform in colour. Spoon into glasses or ramekins and refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving.

items.cause: The cream was over-whipped before the mango was folded in, or the folding was too vigorous.
items.fix: Stop whipping the cream at soft peaks, it should just hold its shape when the whisk is lifted. Fold with slow, sweeping movements rather than stirring.

items.symptom: Gelatine set unevenly, rubbery streaks in the mousse
items.cause: The dissolved gelatine cooled too fast and began to set before it was incorporated into the main purée.
items.fix: Work quickly when mixing the warm gelatine purée back into the bulk. Stir vigorously to distribute it evenly before it starts to set.

items.symptom: Flavour is flat or not very tropical
items.fix: Use the ripest available mangoes, skin should be giving to gentle pressure. Add an extra teaspoon of lemon juice to brighten a flat-tasting purée.

content.text: Keeps covered in the fridge for up to 2 days. The mousse firms slightly on day two. Do not freeze.
